newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIAN RULES AFL-Victorian court delays hearing on Swans player Dunkley.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIAN RULES AFL-Victorian court delays hearing on Swans player Dunkley.

text.p: The Victorian Supreme Court on Wednesday agreed to a request by the Sydney Swans to delay until Thursday morning an Australian Football League (AFL) misconduct hearing into star player Andrew Dunkley, Swans officials said.
The AFL on Wednesday charged Dunkley with misconduct after an incident involving Essendon utlity player James Hird in the first quarter of last Saturday's semifinal between Sydney and Essendon.
The AFL Tribunal hearing had been set down for 7.30 p.m. on Wednesday, three hours after the AFL told Sydney it intended to charge Dunkley.

A statement released by the AFL said it had investigated the incident, after which Hird left the field with a cut under his left eye, and had decided to charge Dunkley with misconduct "for allegedly striking Hird with a left fist to the head".
Sydney officials went to the Victorian Supreme Court seeking an injunction delaying the hearing, arguing that they did not have enough time to prepare for the case.
The court agreed later on Wednesday to grant the injunction.
"The destabilising effect this has had on the Swans over the past four days just can't be understated," Swans chairman Richard Colless told reporters.
Dunkley is due to play his 100th senior AFL game in Saturday's grand final against North Melbourne.
Hird and Brisbane's Michael Voss on Monday were named as joint winners of this year's Brownlow medal for the best and fiarest AFL player.
